top_choice_rationale: P001 (Mircea Cărtărescu, single writer) is my first choice on the common criteria, not on the unanimity of earlier rankings. As publicly described, the voice is distinctive and recognisable, the formal achievement lies in large, densely patterned architectures (Blinding, the first volume of the Orbitor trilogy, and Solenoid), and the imaginative and intellectual depth comes from building memory, the body and dream into one sustained metaphysical project. A poetic origin and essay work suggest an oeuvre broader than the long novels, though my coverage of those parts is thinner and the whole-oeuvre claim is partly inferred. Open reservations remain: how much of the Romanian syntax and rhythm survives in translation, and whether the late, very large volumes deepen the project or only enlarge it. I have no close-reading evidence on either point, and none was supplied in round 2. These limit what a citation can claim; it should rest on the major prose cycles and name Romanian. They do not make no award (P000) preferable, since I find no reason of merit or citation scope to withhold the prize. My assessment rests on public knowledge, not fresh reading or independent verification.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my scholarly work on modern poetry, the fragment, exile literature and Celan translation is context only, and as chair I wrote the round-1 summary, which I disclose without adjudicating
